source.title: Simulating 2D lattice gauge theories on a qudit quantum computer
reproduced_interfaces: Eqs. 9-10: single open plaquette 2D-QED Hamiltonian after Gauss-law elimination
Appendix G Table 1: full gauge one-plaquette register/CNOT resource formulas
Appendix G Table 2: pure-gauge periodic-plaquette register/CNOT resource formulas

single_plaquette_reproduction.solver: deterministic shifted power iteration on the exact finite real-symmetric Hamiltonian
single_plaquette_reproduction.finding: The independent exact finite-dimensional calculation reproduces the source-v3 qualitative strong-to-weak-coupling behavior and approaches the stated d=3 weak-coupling plaquette value 1/sqrt(2).

interpretation.positive_result: A published experimentally grounded particle-physics quantum-simulation route is independently reproducible at the Hamiltonian/resource-interface level, and native qudits give a concrete encoding/circuit-complexity advantage over the paper's comparable one-hot qubit construction for these small circuits.
interpretation.boundary: This is a representation/circuit-resource advantage for a specific small lattice-QED simulation route, not an end-to-end computational or economic quantum advantage.
interpretation.technology_path: elementary-particle/QED theory -> lattice gauge model -> Gauss-law reduction -> native qudit gauge-field encoding -> lower register/entangling-gate burden -> candidate device/runtime primitive
